'''Chris John McGowan''' (born December 1966) is an American political candidate and businessman who has served as the president of the [[Siouxland]] Chamber of Commerce since 2011. He is the member-elect for [[Iowa's 4th congressional district]] in the [[United States House of Representatives]].

==Early life==
McGowan was born in December 1966 in [[Sioux City, Iowa]].<ref>https://www.thegazette.com/news/elections/sioux-city-s-chris-mcgowan-touts-trump-endorsement-in-4th-congressional-district-race/article_ad8399df-99cd-5c0c-9bfa-f1ec1aaefb7b.html</ref><ref>https://www.legistorm.com/person/bio/556262/Christopher_John_McGowan.html</ref>

==Biography==
McGowan has served as President of the Siouxland Chamber of Commerce since 2011.

In 2025, he announced his campaign for [[Iowa's 4th congressional district]] in the 2026 cycle. He gained endorsements from [[Jim Jordan]], [[Steve Scalise]], [[Tom Emmer]], and [[Donald Trump]], and outpaced the primary field in fundraising.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hayworth |first=Bret |title=McGowan of Sioux City leads all Iowa 4th congressional district candidates in fundraising |url=https://www.kwit.org/podcast/spm-news/2026-02-03/mcgowan-of-sioux-city-leads-all-iowa-4th-congressional-district-candidates-in-fundraising |access-date=2026-06-20 |website=Siouxland Public Media |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McNett |first=Jared |date=2026-02-05 |title=Sioux City’s Chris McGowan touts Trump endorsement in 4th Congressional District race |url=https://www.thegazette.com/news/elections/sioux-city-s-chris-mcgowan-touts-trump-endorsement-in-4th-congressional-district-race/article_ad8399df-99cd-5c0c-9bfa-f1ec1aaefb7b.html |access-date=2026-06-20 |website=The Gazette |language=en}}</ref> He was set to [[Matt Windschitl]] and other candidates in the primary<ref>{{Cite web |last=McNett |first=Jared |date=2025-06-25 |title=Siouxland Chamber of Commerce President Chris McGowan running for Congress |url=https://www.thegazette.com/news/elections/siouxland-chamber-of-commerce-president-chris-mcgowan-running-for-congress/article_a1065a97-28d6-5974-be49-0f91be2f550e.html |access-date=2026-06-20 |website=The Gazette |language=en}}</ref>, but ultimately had no opponents.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyckoff |first=Sophie |date=2026-06-04 |title=Dave Dawson outlines next steps after primary win |url=https://www.ktiv.com/2026/06/04/dave-dawson-outlines-next-steps-after-primary-win/ |access-date=2026-06-20 |website=KTIV |language=en}}</ref>

His biography was published in [[The Almanac of American Politics]] as part of the first-ever publication series of candidates who won their party's nomination in seats safe for their party.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Politics |first=Almanac of American |date=2026-06-09 |title=Expected Rep. Chris McGowan (R), Iowa's 4th District |url=https://almanacofamericanpolitics.substack.com/p/expected-rep-chris-mcgowan-r-iowas |access-date=2026-06-20 |website=Almanac of American Politics with Louis Jacobson}}</ref>
